title: Christian Theology & Biblical Studies Scholar Map
purpose: Give the Potato of Life theology layer a broad map of scholars, theologians and primary historical interpreters organized by question rather than treating prestige or one school as authority. Inclusion means useful for research, not endorsement.
use_rule: For any major question, read across disagreement. Prefer primary texts for what historical theologians actually taught, peer-reviewed or academic publications for modern scholarship, and denominational sources for a tradition's current self-description.

research_protocol: Do not use a scholar's name as a substitute for an argument.
For disputed questions, include at least two materially different schools where possible.
Separate theologians speaking confessionally from historians making historical claims.
Separate ancient authors as primary reception-history witnesses from modern scholars analyzing them.
Do not infer that one scholar represents an entire denomination.
For Thomasine, Revelation and historical-Jesus questions, preserve dating/source disagreements rather than choosing one silently.
When Potatoverse material is compared with a scholar's theory, record the exact relation: analogy, explanatory lens, contrast, influence, convergence or independent resemblance.
